title: Improving Officer and Civilian Health
official: Improving Officer and Civilian Health Improving Officer and Civilian Health Through Macro-level Changes in North Texas: Phase 2: Intervention Pilot Testing
summary: As a profession, law enforcement produces unique occupational health outcomes for officers and civilians. To date, most studies have focused on improving health outcomes related to law enforcement from a microlevel perspective, with particular attention to individual and behavioral factors. Such a focus misses the broader macro-level factors that perpetuate occupational harms. To address this gap, this study uses the PRECEDE-PROCEED model of intervention development to examine modifiable macro-level factors contributing to adverse occupational health outcomes for law enforcement and civilians. Using a mixed-method design and partnering with local law enforcement agencies, the investigators will implement and test an intervention to reduce occupational health harms related to law enforcement.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

1. All Aims: Individuals who speak English.
2. All Aims: Individuals who are at least 18 years or older.
3. Aim 1a, Aim 2a, Aim 2b, Aim 2c: Law enforcement officers from the Tarrant County Sheriff's Department who have been in their role for six months or longer.
4. Aim 1b: Staff members in the Tarrant County District Attorneys in office who have been in their role for one year or longer.
5. Aim 1c: Hospital emergency department staff who have been in their position for at least one year.
6. Aim 1c: Elected officials who have been in their position for at least one year.
7. Aim 1c: 911 Dispatchers who have been in their position for at least one year.
8. Aim 1c: Employees with the Tarrant County mental health authority

Exclusion Criteria:

1. All Aims: Individuals who do not speak English.
2. All Aims: Individuals under the age of 18.
3. Aim 1a, Aim 2a, Aim 2b, Aim 2c: Individuals not currently employed by the Tarrant County Sheriff's Department or have not been employed for at least six months in the department.
4. Aim 1b: District Attorneys outside of Tarrant County or have not been in their position for at least 6 months.
5. Aim 1c: Elected officials who have not been in their position for one year or work outside of Tarrant County.
6. Aim 1c: Hospital emergency department staff who have not been in their position for at least one year.
7. Aim 1c: 911 Dispatchers who have been in their position for at least one year.
8. Aim 1c: Employees with the Tarrant County mental health authority who have not been in their position for at least one year. -
